Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- 42-year-old woman with acute continuous spinning vertigo (≈2 h so far), nausea, tinnitus, and gait unsteadiness without focal neurological deficits.  
- Working diagnosis: Acute vestibular neuritis / viral labyrinthitis (high likelihood per transcript and DDx).  
- Alternative considerations: Ménière’s disease (recurrent vertigo + tinnitus, moderate likelihood); posterior-circulation stroke/TIA (low–moderate likelihood given acute persistent vertigo—no focal deficits but must be excluded if neurological signs develop).  
- Management commenced: Symptomatic medication prescribed (name not documented) “1 tablet TID for 10 days.”  
- Safety-net advice: Seek emergency care if limb weakness, severe headache, or persistent vomiting occur.  
- Follow-up: Arrange face-to-face appointment for physical exam (BP, neurologic gait assessment, otoscopy).
